issue: Off-by-one on the length limit: a trimmed query of exactly 100 characters is rejected, but the spec (AC6) says 100 chars must return 200 and only 101+ returns 400.
evidence: `if (q.length >= MAX_QUERY_LENGTH)` with MAX_QUERY_LENGTH = 100 -> GET /api/books/search?q=<100 a's> returns 400; should be `>`.

issue: No type / single-value validation on q. Repeated or non-string q is coerced by String() instead of returning 400 { error: 'Query must be a single string' }.
evidence: `const q = String(req.query.q ?? '').trim();` -> ?q=a&q=b becomes 'a,b' and returns 200; ?q[x]=1 becomes '[object Object]'. The spec's 'Query must be a single string' error is never produced.

issue: Author matching uses instr(), which is case-sensitive and bypasses the required `LIKE ? ESCAPE '\'` on both columns, breaking AC2/AC3 for authors.
evidence: `OR instr(author, ?) > 0` with params `[pattern, query]` -> q=fowler does not match seed author 'Martin Fowler', so 'Refactoring' is missing from results.

issue: Underscore is not escaped, so `_` acts as a LIKE wildcard on title, violating AC8 (q=_ must return [] on seed). The spec requires escaping \, % and _.
evidence: `query.replace(/\\/g, '\\\\').replace(/%/g, '\\%')` has no `_` replacement -> q=_ yields pattern `%_%`, which matches every non-empty title.

issue: Tests cover only part of AC1-AC9 (AC10): nothing for author match (AC2), the 100-char boundary (AC6), literal % / _ (AC8), repeated/non-string q, the exact error message, or route precedence over /books/:id (AC9) - which is why the bugs above pass.
evidence: File has 4 tests only: q=CLEAN title match, whitespace -> all, ' OR 1=1 -- -> [], 101 chars -> 400 with toHaveProperty('error'). No q=fowler, 100-char, q=%, q=_, or ?q=a&q=b case.
